Question Choices: What is the population in a statistical study?
Question Answers: the entire group of interest|all individuals of interest|the full group being studied
Hints: The population is broader than the sample.;It is the group the study aims to describe.
Solution: The population is the entire group of interest.

Question Answers: a subset of the population|part of the population
Hints: Researchers often cannot measure everyone.;They collect data from a smaller group.
Solution: A sample is a subset of the population.

Question Choices: Why is a random sample useful?
Question Answers: it reduces selection bias|it gives each member a chance to be selected|it can better represent the population
Hints: Selection should not favor one group.;Random choice improves representativeness.
Solution: A random sample reduces selection bias.

Question Choices: A school surveys only students in the chess club about homework time. Is this sample likely biased? Enter Yes or No.
Hints: The sample leaves out most students.;Club members may differ from others.
Solution: Yes — the sample is not representative of all students.

Question Choices: A study of 500 voters selected at random from a city aims to describe all city voters. Which group is the sample?
Hints: The sample is the measured subset.;The population is all city voters.
Solution: The 500 selected voters form the sample.
